invariants.evidence: Capability is added behind the single soil-water solver architecture; no separate SWAP kernel/version is introduced.
No file I/O, parser, unit number or path enters the directional seam.
Directional request/result data is explicitly separate from physical state, forcing, parameters and numerical config.
No derivative/tangent vector is added to persistent per-column physical state.
Captured factorization, RHS and directional vectors remain worker/job scratch.
Contract does not constrain internal storage to per-column heavy objects; scratch remains reusable per worker.
Only an accepted physical step may publish AVAILABLE; retry/nonacceptance publishes no accepted outgoing direction. Multi-step rollback ownership remains F-KT.
No committed physical origin is modified by sensitivity evaluation; physical solve ON/OFF identity is a qualification gate.
Derivative uses generic step_duration; no day/month/year boundary is introduced.
One-step primitive is independent of coupling-window placement or midnight boundaries; whole-window composition remains downstream.
Accepted-step sensitivity is designed for coupling composition but F-SI37 does not itself claim predictor-corrector or whole-window coupling.
No groundwater H/q interface sign or tolerance contract is changed.
Sensitivity cannot relax mass acceptance; mode-5 qbot direction differentiates the exact mass-consistent publication algebra.
Accepted-step interface sensitivity becomes a first-class optional result using the accepted factorization; LOCAL_TERMINAL semantics are preserved separately.
Normal available path requires zero extra full nonlinear trajectories and one O(N) tridiagonal backsolve per scalar direction.
No solver instance is stored per column; tangent scratch is worker-owned and therefore compatible with MultiSWAP batching.
No MODFLOW cell/tile mapping assumption is added.
Deep-vadose remains external and unrelated to this solver-side primitive.
No component transition or stored-water transfer semantics are modified.
Alternative soil-water solvers can return sensitivity unavailable without emulating Richards internals.
Directional code differentiates/reuses existing SWAP constitutive and surface-process semantics rather than duplicating a new physical model.
HeadCalc arrays do not escape the solver boundary; consumer sees only the typed directional request/result.
No physical option is changed by numerical sensitivity policy; nonsmooth physics simply makes sensitivity unavailable.
Sensitivity cost is bounded; failure/unavailable routes do not launch repeated production trajectories.
Reference Full Richards physical solve remains unchanged and is the qualification oracle target.
Result carries method, route, availability and explicit extra backsolve/Jacobian/nonlinear-solve diagnostics; trajectory diagnostics remain downstream F-KT.
Directional work is opt-in; unused solves/columns pay no persistent memory cost.
No tile fractions, aquifer mapping or system composition is moved into SWAP kernel/solver.
Control coordinate, route eligibility, smoothness and unavailable conditions are explicit; no midnight, file-format or MODFLOW assumption appears.
Architecture, derivation, cost, fail-closed behavior and downstream ownership are explicitly audited; final owner-qualified decision still requires the green executable gate.
